title: Tunable electronic interactions in small lanthanide(III) nanoclusters: The comparative effects of OH− and O2− supramolecular glues on europium(III)-to-dysprosium(III) energy transfer

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.formula: [Ln2(μ2-L)2(L)4]·nH2O (n = 0–3; L = 2,6-diformyl-p-cresolate; Ln = Pr–Tb except Pm, Er, Tm, Y); crystallographically determined [Pr2(μ2-L)2(L)4]

synthesis.procedure: 0.12 mmol Ln(ClO4)3·nH2O in 20 mL ethanol was added to a mixture of 0.35 mmol HL (2,6-diformyl-p-cresol) and 0.35 mmol NaOH in 25 mL methanol. The clear yellow solution was left to evaporate slowly on a hotplate at 60 °C. For Ln = Pr–Sm anhydrous solvents were used. Heteronuclear complexes were prepared analogously with the desired metal-ion percentages. After one day yellow rod-like crystals of 1 were recovered. Single crystals of 1 (Ln = Pr and Y) were collected on a Siemens P4 diffractometer.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: yellow rod-like crystals recovered after one day; best grown from anhydrous ethanolic solutions of rare-earth perchlorates and HL at about 60 °C

properties.summary: Excitation/emission and 77 K Eu(5D0) decay kinetics of homo- and heterodinuclear [(EuxLn1−x)2(μ2-L)2(L)4] show intramolecular Eu–Ln energy transfer that is often too fast to resolve, plus weaker intermolecular quenching. Eu–Yb quenching is unusually efficient and assigned to phonon-assisted coupling of Eu(5D0) and Yb(2F7/2) with C=O and other vibrations; IR shows a broad carbonyl band at 1660 cm−1 and NIR Yb absorption at 930 and 1043 nm.

synthesis.procedure: 0.18 mmol Ln(ClO4)3·nH2O in 20 mL ethanol was added to a mixture of 0.35 mmol HL and 0.35 mmol NaOH in 25 mL methanol. For the Eu(III) analogue the lanthanide salt was added to HL/NaOH in 25 mL methanol plus 20 mL butan-2-ol. The clear yellow solution was left to evaporate slowly on a hotplate at 80 °C. Yellow needle-like crystals were recovered after 3 days. Series members include Ln = Y, Eu–Lu with X = ClO4− or CF3SO3−. The Ho complex was the crystallographically determined representative.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: yellow needle-like crystals recovered after 3 days

properties.summary: Eu-doped members of series 2 show 77 K Eu(5D0) luminescence and energy transfer to Dy or Yb. Polar μ2-OH bridges couple Eu–Ln less efficiently than μ3-OH in series 3 but more efficiently than phenolate-only dinuclear 1. Fast-component decay for [(Dy0.81Eu0.19)4(μ4-O)(μ2-OH)2(μ2-L)6]2+ is 1.7×10^5 s−1.

synthesis.procedure: 2 mmol NaOH in 10 mL methanol was added in 5 portions to a boiling solution of 8 mmol Ln(ClO4)3·nH2O in 10 mL methanol. A solution of 4 mmol HL and 4 mmol NaOH in 150 mL methanol was then added in 20 mL portions; after each addition the mixture was boiled until ~10 mL remained. The final mixture (pH ≈ 6.5) was evaporated to 5 mL, cooled, filtered, and ~10 mL ethanol added. The mixture was left in an open flask at room temperature. Yellow cubic crystals of 3 were recovered after 5 days. Series members: Ln = Pr–Eu; X = ClO4− or CF3SO3−. The Eu complex was the crystallographically determined representative (Nonius Kappa CCD).

reagents.name: sodium hydroxide
reagents.amount: 2 mmol in 10 mL methanol plus 4 mmol with HL

synthesis.temperature: boiling methanol, then room temperature crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: evaporated to 5 mL, cooled, filtered, ~10 mL ethanol added; yellow cubic crystals after 5 days at room temperature

properties.summary: Series 3 shows the strongest Eu–Dy electronic coupling of the three families, attributed to highly polar μ3-OH glues. Fast Eu(5D0) decay for [(Dy0.22Eu0.78)4(μ3-OH)4(μ2-L)4]4+ is 6.3×10^5 s−1. Each additional Dy on an Eu–OH unit is estimated to contribute kμOH ≈ 1.9×10^4 s−1 to OH-mediated dipole–dipole energy transfer.

measurements.name: OH-mediated Eu-to-Dy energy-transfer increment kμOH
measurements.conditions: per Dy3+ added to an Eu–OH unit; derived from Table 2/Fig. 10 analysis
